samples.question: Exactly two of the small square chips in this picture are drawn with a black border; all the other chips are drawn with a gray border. Each chip is divided into a 5 by 5 grid of 25 equal square cells, and every cell is filled with one of just two tones, a darker tone and a lighter tone. The three-square key near the bottom left shows those two tones with their exact midpoint tone between them. Carry out this operation on the two black-bordered chips: lay one chip exactly on top of the other so their borders coincide, and mark every one of the 25 grid positions whose tone differs between the two black-bordered chips. Marked positions are exactly the positions where one chip is darker and the other is lighter; positions where both chips agree stay unmarked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. Neither black-bordered chip shows the symbol on its own, and the gray-bordered chips and the key are decoration. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell.
